exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). Ask the student about the place where they live, one question at a time: Do you live in a village, a town, or a city? Where is it? How big is it? What’s the population? What’s it like? What is there to see? React to each answer. If the student can’t continue, give an example about your own city in the same way as the book’s example: ‘York is a city in the north of England, on the River Ouse. It’s about 25 miles east of Leeds. It’s a medium-sized city with a population of about 200,000. It’s famous for its cathedral.’ At the end ask which places (a castle, a market, a harbour, a museum…) are there or aren’t there in their town.

exercises.opener: So, tell me about where you live. Do you live in a village, a town, or a city?

says how big it is and the population with a correct number
uses at least three adjectives from the lesson (noisy, polluted, historic, safe…)
names at least three places to see (cathedral, market, castle, bridge…)

reference.title: Examples
rows: Tokyo is the cleanest capital city in the world.
Spain is one of the most popular holiday destinations.
Camping is the least expensive way to go on holiday.
It’s the most beautiful city I’ve ever been to.
It’s the best film I’ve seen this year.

reference.title: in, the least
reference.text: After superlatives we use in + names of places or singular words for groups of people: It’s the noisiest city in the world. Ann’s the oldest in the class. We can also use the least + adjective: the least expensive = the cheapest.

reference.title: superlative + ever + present perfect
reference.text: We often use the + superlative with the present perfect + ever: It’s the most beautiful city I’ve ever been to. What’s the best film you’ve ever seen?

reference.wrong: It’s the noisiest city of the world.
reference.right: It’s the noisiest city in the world.
reference.why: Use in with places and groups.

reference.wrong: It’s the best film I ever saw.
reference.right: It’s the best film I’ve ever seen.

reference.title: Ranking things in order
reference.text: Things are normally ranked from first to last. If two things have the same ranking, e.g. if they are both second, they are called joint second, etc. USA won the most Olympic medals. China and Germany were joint second (= they won the same number of medals).

reference.title: Describing where you live
reference.text: Useful phrases: It’s near the famous… · There are a lot of… · for example… · … is typical of… · It’s famous for… · … is the symbol of the city · It has many local specialities like… · What I like best about… is…

tasks.context:
What are the most (and least) honest cities in the world? Reader’s Digest organized an experiment to try to find out…

Their reporters ‘lost’ 12 wallets in 16 cities around the world. They left the wallets in different areas of each of the chosen cities, places like shopping malls, or in parks, or on the pavement. In each wallet there was the equivalent of 50 dollars in local currency, a family photo, and a couple of business cards with a name and phone number. A reporter waited somewhere near each wallet to see what happened. Another reporter answered the phone when people called to report the lost wallet, and then met the people and asked them why they returned the wallet.

says what was in the wallets (money, a family photo, business cards)

tasks.instruction: Think about your city. In this experiment, would it come in the top three, the bottom three, or somewhere in the middle? Why?
tasks.note: SB 3e → Talk

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). You both listened to the results of the Reader’s Digest lost wallet experiment: reporters ‘lost’ 12 wallets in each of 16 cities; Helsinki was first (11 wallets returned), Mumbai second, Lisbon last (only one). Ask the student: if the experiment happened in their city (or the nearest big city), would it come in the top three, the bottom three, or somewhere in the middle? Why? Then ask: Have you ever found or lost a wallet? What happened? Share your own short opinion and story.
exercises.goal: Would your city be honest in the experiment?
exercises.opener: So, what do you think? If they did the experiment in your city, would it come in the top three?
criteria: gives a clear opinion (top three / bottom three / in the middle)
gives at least two reasons
uses at least one superlative (the most honest, the friendliest)
tells a short story in the past if they have one

tasks.context:
1 I live in Kayseri, which is an important city in Central Anatolia in Turkey. It has a population of over 1,000,000 people. It’s near the famous Cappadocia area, so there are a lot of tourists in the summer.
2 Kayseri is one of the richest cities in Turkey because it has a lot of industry. It is a university town with four universities. There are also many historic buildings, for example Kayseri Castle, Hunat Hatun Mosque, and the Grand Bazaar. But Kayseri also has modern residential areas full of luxury blocks of flats, shopping centres, and stylish restaurants.
3 The weather in Kayseri is typical of the Middle Anatolia Region. Winters are cold and snowy – great for skiing – and summers are hot and dry.
4 Kayseri is famous for its mountains. Mount Erciyes is the symbol of the city and it has a well-known ski resort. It’s also famous for its food and has many local specialities.
5 What I like best about Kayseri is that we are so close to nature.
